To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the columnar aerosol optical depth in the UV spectral range can be estimated from measurements in the visible and infrared spectral regions, 2) the estimation is more accurate in continental areas than in maritime areas, 3) the estimation error is lower in summer than in winter, 4) the estimation error increases with the aerosol optical depth and 5) the error is larger for the UV-A spectral region than for the UV-B region.
The columnar optical depth at UV and visible wavelengths has been measured in two different areas of Spain.
(1) The aerosol optical depth of the tropospheric aerosolic load is a key factor in determining the amount of UV radiation reaching the ground.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the atmospheric aerosols and its effects on the radiation field in the UV spectral range.
the study of the atmospheric aerosols in the ultraviolet spectral region.
the study of the optical characteristics of tropospheric atmospheric aerosols.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the columnar troposheric aerosol optical depth is higher in the coastal area (Gulf of Cadiz) than in the continental area (northern Spain), and the aerosol optical depth in the UV range is higher than in the visible range, with the exception of some days of the year.
the aerosol optical depth in the UV region is a key parameter in order to understand the behaviour of the UV radiation reaching the Earth surface.

(1) the Angstrom method is the best method to estimate aerosol optical depth in the UV range; (2) the correlation method is a good tool to estimate aerosol columnar optical depth in the visible range; (3) in both cases the error is of the order of 20–30% in the visible and 50–60% in the UV region; (4) the aerosol type seems to be the most important factor to determine the quality of the estimation;
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the aerosols optical depth at 350nm is a function of the aerosol optical depth in the visible region, the Angstrom turbidities in the visible and the Angstrom turbidiity in the UV region.
the columnar optical properties of tropospheric UV aerosols are very variable in space and time and can be estimated from the Angstrom turbidty parameter and/or the correlation between wavelengths.
we have developed a method for the estimation of the aerosol optical depth in the UV region, which is the most sensitive region to the effects of aerosols in the atmosphere.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aerosol optical depth can be estimated with a good accuracy at UV wavelengths based only on the information in the visible region, at least at the two stations studied.
the aerosol optical depth (AOD) at the UV range can be estimated from measurements at the visible range with a reasonable accuracy (±0.05) for continental sites.
the Angstrom turbidty parameter method, which has been widely used to estimate the aerosol optical depth in the UV region, can be used to obtain reasonable values of the UV aerosol optical depth.
